assignment:
Some of your friends perform community service. For example, some tutor elementary school children and others clean up litter. They think helping the community is very important. But other friends of yours think community service takes too much time away from what they need or want to do. 
Your principal is deciding whether to require all students to perform community service. 
Write a letter to your principal in which you take a position on whether students should be required to perform community service. Support your position with examples.
essay_1:
Dear Principal,

I am writing about whether every student should have to do community service. I think our school should make it a requirement, but it has to be flexible because students are already really busy.

Some of my friends already volunteer, and I have seen what it does for them. My friend Maya tutors second graders in reading every Tuesday after school. At first she only signed up because her mom made her. Now she talks about her students all the time, and she tells everyone when one of them finishes a chapter book. She is more patient now and she can talk in front of people without shaking. Another friend, Daniel, joined a group that cleans trash out of the creek behind the shopping center on weekends. He told me he had no idea how much garbage was in our town until he spent a morning pulling bottles and plastic bags out of the water. It was so gross, but he kept going. Now he picks up trash even when nobody is watching. You can hear about responsibility in class, but doing it yourself teaches it better.

I also get why other students are against the idea. A lot of us have jobs, sports practice, music lessons, or little brothers and sisters to watch at home. Homework already takes hours every night. If the school made us do fifty hours a semester, some kids would fall behind or stay up too late, and the service would feel like a punishment. That would be really unfair.

That is why I think the requirement should be reasonable. Maybe twenty hours a year would be enough, and students could pick when and how to do them. Someone who works on weekdays could help at a food bank on Saturday. An athlete could coach a kids team during the off-season. The school could even count things students already do, like working at a church event or reading to patients at the hospital. If students get to choose, the hours would feel very real instead of forced.

A requirement would also help kids who would stay home otherwise because they have no clue where to start. Some people only find out they like helping after they try it, but they need someone to push them first.

Our town gives us a lot, like parks, libraries, and teachers. A small requirement that works with our schedules would teach students to give something back. It will take some planning, but I think it is worth it. I hope you will think about it.

Sincerely,
A concerned student

Dear Principal,

I am writing about if every student should have to do community service. I think our school should make it a rule, but it should be flexable because kids are already really busy.

Some of my friends already volunteer and I seen what it does for them. My friend Maya helps second graders with reading every Tuesday after school. At first she only did it because her mom made her. Now she talks about "her kids" all the time and she gets super excited when one of them finishes a chapter book. She is more patient now and she isnt as scared to talk in front of people. My other friend Daniel goes with a group on weekends that picks up trash in the creek behind the shopping center. He said he never knew how much trash was in our town until he spent a whole morning pulling bottles and plastic bags out of the water. Now he picks up trash even when nobody is looking. Stuff like that teaches you responsibility in a way sitting in class cant.

But I also get why some kids dont like the idea. Alot of us have jobs, sports practice, music lessons, or little brothers and sisters to babysit. Homework already takes forever every night. If the school made us do like fifty hours a semester some kids would fall behind or not get enough sleep, and it would feel like a punishment instead of helping. That kind of ruins the whole point.

Thats why I think the rule should be reasonable. Maybe twenty hours a year would be enough, and students could pick when and how they do it. If someone works on weekdays they could help at a food bank on Saturday. If someone plays a sport they could coach a little kids team in the off season. The school could even count stuff kids already do, like helping at a church event or reading to people at the hospital. If students get to choose then the hours would actually mean something and not feel forced.

Making it required would also help kids who would never volunteer on there own just because they dont know how to start. Alot of people only find out they like helping after they try it.

Our community gives us alot, like parks, libraries, and teachers. A small flexable requirement would teach students to give back. I hope you think about it.

Sincerely,
A concerned student
